title: Project and Pack methods
summary: yoke qa mission host-command --timeout-seconds defaults to 60 and allows at most 900. A --gui-session command that times out has its whole process tree stopped, returns the stdout and stderr it printed before the deadline, and reports gui_command_timeout_stopped as the last stderr line; when it cannot be confirmed gone it reports gui_command_timeout_not_stopped, keeps its output files and names their paths. A Terminal window left open is named gui_command_window_not_closed beside the command's own answer. A Yoke setup, connect or onboard call with a timeout under the 600s browser-approval wait prints the warning host_command_timeout_below_approval_wait; agent mode (--agent or --answer) returns its next question without waiting and gets no warning. After deployment membership removal, the original execution session can run walk-end on the recorded host under a temporary cleanup lease; teardown deletes staged secrets, restores starting state and records proof while the execution stays aborted. Other sessions, walk-start and host-command remain refused. Guards exempt host-command argv only on a direct call, so a walker never wraps it in its own script. The supported pull step is `-- base64 -i REMOTE_PATH > LOCAL.json`, then decoding the JSON stdout field locally. A refused target in another user's home from a call with no `yoke` invocation names that direct call. A mission host-command can select a companion declared in method_config.test_machines with --test-machine NAME; omission targets the retained driver. The server validates all host leases, refuses outside hosts with mission_machine_not_declared, and issues a host_command contract for the companion lease without reset or secret staging. Walk setup, scratch and teardown remain on the driver. Self-host first-boot tokens originate on the companion and stay in its owner-only bundle secrets directory until cleanup. Companion command authority records durable reset debt before local execution, including commands that fail after partial mutation. The debt survives driver walk-end and companion lease release until a verified reset to the owed baseline clears it; untouched companions acquire no debt from driver access. Walk-end, on a finished or aborted walk, only removes owner-only secret staging, restores the starting state and records that restore; it never tracks or removes what the walk created. The walker cleans up everything it creates (repositories, accounts, records the product registered) with the product's own commands and reports anything it could not remove.
